correctness.rationale: For arbitrary fixed-mass Borel vaccine measures, the integral susceptible formula has a constant denominator and a strictly convex exponential-arc integrand. Sensitivity of the pure-pulse orbit yields switching value S(t)v(t), whose endpoint derivatives reduce exactly to z≥B/[βH(1-r)] and z≥βL(1-r)/B. High-season strict concavity of G and low-season derivative monotonicity prove these endpoint tests sufficient over the entire circle. Violation gives a strictly improving arbitrarily small mass relocation. An independently implemented two-pulse exact affine-integral checker reproduces directional derivatives and both opposite side examples. No inference from finite grid to global optimum is used.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison with the motivating 2026 numerical square-wave vaccination example and the authors’ 2026 general convexity/optimality paper. The source reports approximately 0.4 but not an exact threshold; the general paper is credited for convexity, uniqueness and the first-order criterion. New mathematical step is the sharp necessary-and-sufficient threshold across every positive two-season configuration and an exact comparison of two possible one-sided losses. Relevant published research records did not show a statement implying these formulas. Residual risk for unindexed equivalents remains.

value.rationale: The motivating epidemiological paper treats the practical pure-pulse to mixed-control transition as a numerical observation. This theorem gives its exact cutoff against all nonnegative measure-valued policies, not only computational grids, and a general two-mechanism parameter phase boundary. The result provides a quantitative benchmark and clarifies when vaccine dose should first be spread before versus after high-season onset; it does not make unsupported endemic-case claims.
